title: Traffic, Transport & Road Closures – TCS Sydney Marathon
claims: Participants in the Purple and Orange assembly groups are directed to North Sydney Station by train, while Green assembly group runners connect by metro to Crows Nest.
The nearest metro stations to the start venue are Victoria Cross Station and Crows Nest Station, depending on start group, and early morning metro services will run.

Participants in Purple and Orange groups should reach Victoria Cross metro and exit via Denison Street, then Walker Street, while Green group runners should reach Crows Nest and use the Clarke Street exit.

Metro services connect with the CBD from Central, Gadigal, Martin Place and Barangaroo stations; from the north, change at Chatswood or Epping, and from the south or west change at Sydenham or Central.
Buses will be heavily impacted by event road closures, the closest stops to the start area will be around Crows Nest, and limited buses will stop along Falcon Street near St Leonards Park.
Light rail services will run from 3:45am on all lines, including L1 Dulwich Hill, L2 Randwick and L3 Kingsford, and L3 services will not operate from Kingsford after 5:47am.
A dedicated drop-off area will be available at ANZAC Public School on Anzac Avenue off Ernest Street, with an accessible drop-off in the North Sydney Boys High School car park on Falcon Street.
The organiser states that public transport is the only way to travel on race morning because of extensive road closures and zero parking in the start and finish zones.
Critical course lock-down is from 5:30am to 10:30am, with major roads closed across Sydney CBD, The Rocks, Walsh Bay, Dawes Point, Millers Point, Barangaroo, Darling Harbour and Pyrmont.

The start area on Miller Street is serviced by three railway stations, each capable of moving 25,000 people per hour into the starting corrals, and runners are asked to arrive at least 60 minutes before their wave start.
The official 2026 marathon bib can be shown to transport staff on all Sydney Trains, metro, bus and ferry services on event Sunday.
Spectators can reach the major spectator and entertainment zones at Customs House, Circular Quay and Mrs Macquarie's Chair by light rail or metro.
